messages:
miriam (engsec): morning folks — quick async checkin for today. please post: what you did yesterday / blockers / what you're tackling today. flagged items: kms rotation dry-run, iam policy audit, and 3 outstanding vuln PRs.

raj (infra): yesterday — finished the IAM policy diff for service accounts (PR #492). blocker — still need approvals from infra-app team. today — pinging them and updating docs. @taylor can you PTAL at the service-account naming comments?

miriam (engsec): thanks raj. linking the PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/492 — main concern is the broad role on analytics-svc. we should scope it to ReadOnly and assume-role.

raj (infra): noted, I'll change to assume-role + scoped permissions. will add a test in staging to verify access.

olivia (compliance): quick note — SOC2 checklist: key rotation proof required for KMS this quarter. do we have a timeline?

miriam (engsec): KMS rotation dry-run completed in staging yesterday. results: no unexpected decrypt failures, but one integration (billing-export) read key from an old alias. blocked on a config change there.

taylor (platform): I can take the billing-export config update. question — do we rotate aliases or create new keys and update aliases? last run used alias swap to minimize downtime.

miriam (engsec): prefer alias swap for low-latency cutover. steps we used in dry-run:
```
# create new key
aws kms create-key --description "rotation-dryrun-2026-03"
# create new alias
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/apps/primary-v2 --target-key-id <new-key-id>
# update services to use alias/apps/primary-v2
# once validated, point alias/apps/primary -> target-key-id for cutover
```

taylor (platform): thanks — I'll schedule the alias swap in canary window today at 17:00 UTC and announce on #incidents if anything unusual.

miriam (engsec): great. raj — can you follow-up on the PR approvals before the canary? if billing-export changes land after the keys swap we risk mismatch.

raj (infra): yup, I'll chase the approvers. also flagging PR #499 (vuln fix) — tests flaked in CI, need someone to rerun.

ci-bot: build status for PR #499 — flaky integration test in connect_test.py. Rerun suggested.

olivia (compliance): manual evidence required after rotation. miriam, can you capture the dry-run logs and upload to the compliance folder? I need them for audit.

miriam (engsec): will do. uploading to S3/compliance/kms-rotations/dryrun-2026-03-15.zip and will paste link here when done.

raj (infra): one more blocker — the IAM audit tool flagged two legacy roles with wildcard permissions in staging. low priority but we should remove them before prod rotation. adding a follow-up ticket.

miriam (engsec): agree. created ticket INFSEC-731 to track legacy role removal + verification plan. assigning to raj.

taylor (platform): today I'll also run the KV cache warmup job post-rotation in staging to validate token flows. estimate 2 hours.

olivia (compliance): FYI legal asked if we keep rotation logs for 1 year — confirmed retention is 13 months in our policy, so good.

miriam (engsec): final asks: 1) raj — get PR approvals, rerun CI for #499 once tests fixed; 2) taylor — proceed with canary alias swap at 17:00 UTC and report any decrypt errors; 3) olivia — I'll upload dry-run logs and update SOC2 checklist. post any updates here. :thumbsup:

raj (infra): on it. ping me if approvers don't respond in 30m, I'll escalate.

taylor (platform): will post canary status in this thread after the swap.

miriam (engsec): uploaded logs: s3://redwood-compliance/kms-rotations/dryrun-2026-03-15.zip

ci-bot: rerun triggered for PR #499 by raj at 1932501500.

raj (infra): CI green on #499 after rerun. merging after a quick changelog update.

miriam (engsec): merging looks good. thanks everyone. will circle back in next async.
